findings: THE TRADE, IN ONE LINE. At fixed geometry, one phase and equal springs, 34 -> 30 costs +12.86 % of the 90th percentile (0.638498565 -> 0.720607136) and buys 68.9x of plan margin (0.025609823 -> 1.764511930 nm). Both readings are past T-5b's 0.10 by 6.4x and 7.2x, so the move is between two designs neither of which is flat under the measured dropout.

THE CHEAP BOUND GOT THE SIGN AND THE SCALE AND UNDER-PREDICTED THE SIZE BY 4.2x. C-0089's six abstract-grid points fit a slope of -0.241246026, which predicts +3.07 % for 34 -> 30 before a single realisation is drawn; the measured cost at fixed geometry is +12.86 %. One division over a published table therefore settles the DIRECTION of CH-0103's trade and the order of its magnitude for nothing, and the sampler is what supplies the factor — which is the honest reading of a cheap bound run before an expensive calculation.

THE COUNT AXIS SURVIVES AT FIXED GEOMETRY, AND IT IS STEEPER THAN THE ABSTRACT GRID'S. Over the two NESTED chains the 90th percentile is monotone decreasing in the count, and the searched family — which moves the placement at every count and is therefore not fixed geometry — is NOT monotone. The readings are chain A — C-0072's own inter: 1.0345 0.9351 0.7983 0.7206 0.6385 0.6322; chain B — the centro-symmetr: 0.9731 0.9542 0.8630 0.7206 0.6385 0.6339; searched — a subset descent : 0.4646 0.5469 0.4507 0.4188 0.4106 0.5414. C-0089 measured 0.85219673 -> 0.532748246 over 15 -> 90 paths on the abstract grid, a slope of -0.241246; the real upward lattice at fixed geometry gives -0.740087, -0.704431, 0.061035. C-0098 found the shared body's lattice slope 2.08x SHALLOWER than its abstract one; the array's runs the other way.

UNDER THE DROPOUT MOST OF THIS FAMILY IS A NET DISHING SOURCE, AND THE SPARSE END IS THE WORST OF IT. The uncoupled tile on this host dishes 0.307902368 of the stroke; 21 of the 21 graded cells exceed it at the 90th percentile, the worst by 3.36x. CLAUDE.md's sign rule — an attachment coupling is a net dishing source below an attachment pitch of one Winkler bending length — is what a dropout walks a design into, and a count reduction starts it closer to the crossing.

THE CHEAP RANKING INSTRUMENT TRANSFERS ACROSS COUNTS AND IT IS THE STRONG DIRECTION. Spearman rho between the worst single removal and the 90th percentile is 0.942857, 1.000000, 0.942857 within a fixed-geometry chain and 1.000000, 1.000000, 1.000000, 1.000000, 1.000000, 0.500000 across placements at one count, against C-0089's 0.972896669 across designs and C-0098's 0.468487481 across phases. So the axis C-0098 found the bound failing on is the PHASE, not the count: the bound tracks a monotone density axis and does not track a lattice reshuffle at fixed density.

THE PLACEMENT AXIS AT FIXED COUNT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE COUNT AXIS AT FIXED PLACEMENT. At 34 paths the three placements read 0.638499, 0.638499, 0.410574 of the stroke, a spread of 1.56x, where the whole 34 -> 30 count move is 1.13x. The variable CH-0103 says the programme spent is the SMALLER of the two on this lattice.

THE CONFOUND IS MEASURED AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF C-0089's REVERSAL. The move the programme actually recommends — C-0063's 34 at phase 24 to C-0074's 30 at phase 8 — reads 0.639129638 -> 0.583664426, i.e. -8.68 %, where the SAME count move at fixed geometry reads +12.86 %. The difference is the PHASE, and it runs the favourable way: CH-0103's own caveat that the 30-root design reads better for a reason that is not the count is confirmed, and the reason is now a number.

THE COUNT AND THE ARM ARE ONE VARIABLE, SO THE ROBUST END OF THE AXIS IS THE UNBUILDABLE END. Of the 6 swept counts, 22, 25, 28, 30, 34 place with their own self-consistent arm and 45 do not, because C-0075's arm grows with the count at a fixed mandate. The direction CH-0103 says fabrication charges on is therefore the direction the PLAN refuses, and the two constraints are not independent axes of one window.

THE DENSITY THE DROPOUT DEMANDS IS UNREACHABLE AT EVERY SWEPT COUNT, AND IT IS A DIVISION. The widest row of the swept family carries 3 roots at a 13.3333 nm pitch against a 12.8291 nm bending length, and C-0089's run-length arithmetic demands 13 columns — a shortfall of 4.33x at the densest count in the sweep. No count the tile can carry closes it.

A REDUNDANCY SLOPE MEASURED OVER SEARCHED SUBSETS IS NOT A COUNT SLOPE, AND HERE THE TWO DIFFER BY 12.1x. On one lattice, one phase, one topology and one ensemble, the NESTED chains fit -0.740086889 and -0.704431429 and the placement-SEARCHED family fits 0.061034834 — a slope of the wrong sign, because a descent at a low count finds a better placement than a nested subset does and the count effect is absorbed into the search. C-0098's real-lattice slope of -0.376769756 is measured over placement-searched subsets of exactly this kind, and it attributes to the lattice's pitch what a descent's unequal tightness can produce on its own. That is CH-0119.

AND THE SEARCHED ROWS ARE NOT DESIGNS: 5 of the 6 searched cells cannot be given arm directions at their own self-consistent arm length, because the descent optimises a dishing objective that knows nothing about a footprint. A subset search on this lattice is a lower bound on the dishing and NOT a placement claim.

THE VERDICT ON CH-0103. Its cost term is MEASURABLE: the cost is 0.082109 of the stroke against a sampling departure of 2.60e-03. The challenge is UPHELD as a bookkeeping correction — the second term exists, it is adverse, it is 12.86 % at the move the programme took, and no claim in the corpus contained it. The 34 -> 30 RECOMMENDATION SURVIVES on three independent grounds: the trade is 68.9x of plan margin against 1.129x of dishing, i.e. 528 to 1 in ratio; the move the programme ACTUALLY recommends carries a phase change that makes it 8.68 % BETTER under the dropout, not worse; and neither design is flat under the measured dropout at any count the tile can carry, so the axis decides no acceptance verdict.
validity: TRL 1-3. Model-consistent and traceable. The dropout INPUT is C-0087's, which is Strauss et al. (2018) read directly on a plain Rothemund rectangle; nothing derived here is measured.
The motif is NOT demonstrated: a free lever held to a single-layer sheet by one crossover is this programme's own construct (C-0028, C-0029, C-0055).

ONE crossover phase. C-0098 measures the phase axis at 1.95x over all 32 phases on the shared-body topology, so a count effect measured at phase 24 is not a statement about the lattice's whole phase family.

EQUAL springs at every count. The distribution axis is C-0089's (1.30-1.61x on an array) and C-0098's (1.026x on a shared body) and is deliberately not re-swept here, because a distribution is a redistribution of the same sum and would confound the count.

The subset search is a first-improvement descent on an objective whose rank agreement is measured here rather than assumed, so the searched rows are UPPER bounds on what the lattice reaches at those counts.
The arm footprint is REPORTED and never imposed: an arm's length is a function of the count (C-0075), so buildability is a plan axis C-0069/C-0075 own.
T-5b's 0.10 is a CONVENTION, not a physical threshold.

The dishing pipeline, the lattice, the host, the load and the free-tile stroke are C-0058's, C-0063's, C-0087's and C-0089's unchanged, and inherit C-0022's unsourced rim charge and C-0001's single foundation secant.
Single layer, static, 300 K, aqueous 2 mM MgCl2.
openQuestions: Whether the coupling element's own incorporation is the staple's — C-0087's item 2, C-0089's item 1 and C-0098's item 5, unchanged, and still the only route by which this programme keeps a flat tile.
Whether the count effect measured at phase 24 holds at the other 31 phases. C-0098's phase axis is 1.95x on a different topology and nothing here bounds the interaction between the two.

Whether a count sweep with the DISTRIBUTION freed at every count reverses the ordering. The distribution is worth 1.30-1.61x on an array (C-0089) and it is not held equal across counts by any acceptance clause.
What fraction of built tiles a flatness verdict is owed over — C-0087's item 4, unchanged, and the parameter the whole branch is most sensitive to.
